glosses: gift (something given to someone on a special occasion)
donation (material good that someone gives selflessly for social purposes)
gift (received good with a special value of an intangible nature)

examples.text: dar wolności

glosses: gift (something received through a higher power)
gift (very well-mastered skill for which someone has a natural predisposition)

examples.text: -Na ruinie bowiem i niewypłacalności- mówił pan Deklewski- musi skończyć człowiek, który nie pilnuje się jednego fachu i nie umie uszanować darów łaskawej fortuny.
examples.translation: - Не миновать разорения и банкротства человеку, который не держится одного дела и не умеет ценить милостивых даров судьбы, ― говорил Деклевский.

examples.translation: Гоженский имел особый дар всюду проникнуть, играть различные роли, смотря по надобности, и получать нужные сведения.

glosses: Something given to another voluntarily, without charge.

examples.text: She gave him a cell phone as a birthday gift.

“I thank you for the gift, Dr. Yueh,” Paul said, speaking formally. “It will be our secret. If there is a gift or favor you wish from me, please do not hesitate to ask.”
"I . . . need for nothing," Yueh said.
But now I know, but now I really know / Of only one thing I am truly very sure / Love is a gift, love is a gift
She bought the model as a surprise gift for a friend who is a lifelong HST fan and railwayman, and who will soon be celebrating a milestone birthday.
She had a gift for playing the flute.

“[…] it is not fair of you to bring against mankind double weapons! Dangerous enough you are as woman alone, without bringing to your aid those gifts of mind suited to problems which men have been accustomed to arrogate to themselves.”

glosses: The act, right, or power of giving or bestowing.

examples.text: The office is in the gift of the President.

glosses: To give as a gift or donation.
To give away, to concede easily.

examples.text: Chelsea threw away two points when substitute Salomon Kalou gifted Valencia a penalty five minutes from time with a needless handball.
They drove on, every rise in the road lifting their sightline clear of the drystone dykes along the roadside, gifting glimpses of the firth and the islands, the blue peaks of Arran.
